How does Epic Games’ Technical Developer Relations team profile games?

You'll see exactly how we profile, what problems we find, and how we’d go about solving them.

Whether you're shipping your first indie title or scaling a AAA production, you'll come away with actionable insights and a deeper understanding of how to think like Epic’s Technical Developer Relations team.

description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Stockholm, we take a look at the new features of the improved GPU profiler that shipped with UE 5.6, and how the extra information it provides can help when profiling titles for both CPU and GPU performance. 

We also take a deep dive on our modern RHI submission pipeline design. This system is responsible for the threading of renderer work on the CPU, and feeding that work to the GPU. 

Watch to learn about the modern Unreal Engine renderer threading design, which is valuable when analysing Unreal Insights traces for rendering related performance issues.

title: Deep Dive into Customizations With Mutable | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
Mutable is an Unreal Engine plugin for creating character customization systems, enabling dynamic changes to characters and other assets during gameplay. 

While it's primarily used for character customization, Mutable is adaptable to other dynamic content like vehicles, weapons, and props.

In this talk recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, you'll learn what Mutable is, how to use it, and most importantly, how not to use it. 

You'll find out how to take the most advantage of it, and how to avoid the most common pitfalls. The session concludes with a review of real projects that are currently using Mutable, pointing up the different use cases of Mutable and also the lessons learned during development.

Learn more about Unreal Engine here: unrealengine.com
author: Unknown

title: Supervised Settings Downloading: Under the Hood with KWS | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
Supervised Settings are critical to the user experience at Epic Games, ensuring that user and parental preferences for crucial settings are respected cross-platform and even cross-game to ensure a cohesive, consistent, and safe experience in the metaverse.

Come and learn what really happens in the background when Epic's Kids Web Services (KWS) performs a Supervised Settings download, and gain an understanding of the sensitive rock-paper-scissors game that takes place at every login in the service of a positive user experience. The goal of this talk is to give you insight into the process required for every login, including calculation of Supervised Settings and the considerations that need to be made when operating at scale in one of the world's biggest gaming ecosystems.
author: Unknown

title: Shoot Your Shot: Cinematic Pipeline Dating Advice | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
Not in love with your current cinematics workflow? We get it, it's hard to find that perfect spark when building a cinematics pipeline that scales in Unreal Engine. So, it is time we change that! 

Whether you’re creating a feature length animated film or cinematics for your indie game, you can up your game with the new Cinematic Assembly Toolset (CAT), a suite of new tools designed to help you escape the tedium of managing a cinematic pipeline and get back to what really matters: making something unreal. 

In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, we explore new developments in shot management, and how CAT can transform your cinematic workflows (and save you from heartache).

Learn more about Unreal Engine here: unrealengine.com
author: Unknown

title: Building Extensible RPG Systems With the Gameplay Ability System | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
How do you design an RPG system where items, skills, and abilities can change anything? In this talk recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, Ian Cox of Stoic Studio presents a case study about their use of the Gameplay Ability System (GAS) to create modular, scalable gameplay modifications in their RPG brawler ‘Towerborne’.

This session covers practical techniques for mapping RPG elements to GAS primitives; creating perks that can modify anything without overloading designers or programmers; and common pitfalls in RPG perk design with GAS and how to address them.

Learn more about Unreal Engine here: unrealengine.com
author: Unknown

title: Optimizing Unreal Engine’s OpenUSD Workflow with Python | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
OpenUSD is rapidly becoming one of the most efficient solutions for building and managing data within studio pipelines. While Unreal Engine supports exporting data in USD format, its native implementation has certain performance limitations that require customization to fit into a pipeline.

In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, Jonghwan Hwang of Sony Pictures Imageworks demonstrates a high-level concept for integrating Unreal Engine into a studio pipeline using OpenUSD. This includes basic USD export from Unreal Engine with Python, developing scripts to parse assets into USD layers, and adding patch scripts for refining USD data to meet specific pipeline requirements.

Through a case study of a simple film Unreal Engine scene structure, the session showcases how these optimizations enable more effective data exchange between Unreal Engine and other DCC tools.

Learn more about Unreal Engine here: unrealengine.com
author: Unknown

title: Working Smarter in UEFN with Scene Graph | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
This session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025 demonstrates how Fortnite projects can benefit from Scene Graph. 

Watch to learn how to use Scene Graph prefabs and components to create reusable data-oriented designs for your project. 

The session also discusses how Scene Graph prefabs enable creators to reduce Verse code, iterate quickly, and reduce bug count. It also includes a comparison of the amount of Verse code in UEFN projects created both with and without Scene Graph.

Learn more about UEFN here: unrealengine.com/uses/uefn-unreal-editor-for-fortnite

title: TerraCrowds in Action: High-Performance Crowd Simulations with UE | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, Roland Geraerts of uCrowds explores the core design ideas of the TerraCrowds engine, including its integration with Unreal Engine components like MetaHumans and MassAI. 

This session covers memory-oriented design, crowd logic for controlling characters, and the Explicit Corridor Map for efficient pathfinding. Other topics include best practices for writing (memory-oriented) high-performance code, offering insights into achieving speeds up to 100x faster than object-oriented approaches. 

Find out how Geraerts and his team designed an architecture that enables accurate pathfinding where NPCs move naturally and avoid obstacles effectively. You’ll see first-hand how Its multi-level planning architecture—from global route planning to local adjustments—enhances realism and control in simulations.

This session demonstrates how to effectively utilize the software in simulation scenarios and digital twins. Watch to gain hands-on knowledge

title: Building a Data-Driven Interior Configurator Using Lumen and Nanite | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
Cabin Creator is an interior configuration tool used by Gulfstream Aerospace’s sales, design, refurbishment, and customer delivery executive teams. Originally developed to facilitate a continued ability to interact with customers during the COVID 19 crisis, Cabin Creator has expanded over the past five years to become a robust and invaluable tool embedded within the enterprise, generating millions of dollars in revenue through the direct sales of new aircraft, refurbishment upsells, and upgraded material and styling options. 

In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, Josh Triplett and Brian Toler of Gulfstream Aerospace step through the processes used to create a modular, data-driven configurator, a responsive UI, and the use of Lumen and Nanite to power a fully dynamic interior. The session also includes a demonstration of Cabin Creator.

Learn more about Unreal Engine here: unrealengine.com

title: Cross-Platform Modding: Expanding ARK’s UGC Ecosystem with UE5 | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
In 2023, ‘ARK: Survival Ascended’ embraced user-generated content (UGC) and enabled mods originally crafted for PC to become seamlessly playable on consoles, including Xbox and PS5. Now, more than 360 million mods have been downloaded across consoles and PCs, and iconic brands like Power Rangers are going in-game via premium mods.

This session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025 dives into the technical and creative strategies that made this cross-platform leap possible, including leveraging Unreal Engine 5 to integrate in-game mod discovery and management. 

Thomas Williamson of Grove Street Games and Shahar Sorek of Overwolf explain how they maintained platform security, integrated user generated patches, and leveraged Zen Loader for optimal mod packaging. 

Watch to gain insights into building cross-platform compatibility, the challenges of maintaining a unified experience across different devices, and how this approach empowers game studios and creators to foster strong UGC ecosy
author: Unknown

title: Augmenting the Most-Watched Live Events with Unreal Engine | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
Girraphic, an international broadcast and advertising agency, has been fortunate enough to be a part of some of the most-watched streaming events in recent history, from Netflix's Paul vs. Tyson and NFL Christmas Gameday to Amazon's Thursday Night Football series. These broadcasts all share one thing in common: the integration of augmented reality (AR) graphics from Unreal Engine.  

This presentation recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025 looks at how Unreal Engine techniques and workflows fit into the live TV space, revealing the lessons Girraphic learned along the way. The session covers challenges like hardware requirements, scene and graphics layout, multiple camera tracking systems, live control of Unreal Engine, and the choice of HDR vs. SDR.

The session also explores where real-time 3D is going next as it gains backing from forward-thinking streaming partners. This talk is for anyone interested in understanding how Unreal Engine can be used for augmented broadcast graphics, and
author: Unknown

description:

In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, Alex Coulombe of Agile Lens showcases the many modular components, design review capabilities, and various navigation options this underused template offers; with a little elbow grease, you can easily add a wide range of features, from additional menu options to worldwide multiplayer, Pixel Streaming, and even cross-platform compatibility. 

And while this template is developed with enterprise in mind (it has architectural and automotive variants), this session also covers how to use the basic structure of the project for a wide variety of industries, including games!

title: The New Frontiers of Asset Creation | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
New AI tools come out every day promising to instantly generate 2D and 3D assets. At a glance, they're incredibly impressive—but working them into a flexible pipeline is another story. 

In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, Halon Entertainment discusses their work on the short film Chika BOOM! and presents their process of traditional and novel asset creation and rendering—all using Unreal Engine as the backbone of the pipeline.

The talk aims to shine a spotlight on Unreal Engine asset workflows with more potential than ever before.

Learn more about Unreal Engine here: unrealengine.com

title: Taking the Pain Out of Engine Upgrades | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, Keith Judge of Tanglewood Games presents techniques for smoothing out the process of upgrading Unreal Engine and avoiding common pitfalls—even for teams that have made engine modifications. 

The talk aims to inform on how to structure your engine modifications in a way that assists with upgrades, and makes the process less daunting. 

Topics include  how to make your engine modifications merge-friendly, easily togglable, and testable during merging; branching/merging setup; automating as much of the merging/resolving as possible (with Robomerge and other tools); updating modules/plugins that have been moved (e.g. from Experimental to Production); third-party plugins; dealing with deprecation warnings; integrating cherry-picked changes from Epic; and using commandlets to resave assets for the new engine version.

Learn more about Unreal Engine here: unrealengine.com

description:

This talk covers the development and implementation of the UI architecture used, and how Firaxis was able to create the enormous breadth of UI screens the game required, including the ability to share functionality by reducing the complexity of UI creation.

Learn more about using Unreal Engine for game development here: unrealengine.com/uses/games

title: How NASA is Using Immersive Technology for Design and Training | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, NASA presents a deep dive into how Unreal Engine was used to create a VR simulation of the Gateway Space Station. 

The Center for Design and Space Architecture (CDSA) at NASA is dedicated to advancing human-centered design for space exploration. As part of this mission, the CDSA’s Virtual Reality (VR) team has developed a high-fidelity VR simulation of the Gateway Space Station, utilizing Nanite technology to integrate large polygon-count meshes of spaceflight hardware and equipment. 

This cutting-edge VR platform allows for detailed exploration and evaluation of the station’s interior design. Through Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) testing, astronauts simulate daily tasks—such as conducting scientific experiments, retrieving supplies, and preparing meals—replicating real-world scenarios that will occur during the Artemis missions. 

These immersive simulations combine virtual models with astronaut input, providing invaluable insights th
author: Unknown

title: Subculture Rendering and Calculations in Mongil: Star Dive | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, Hyunggoo Kim (Michaelk) of Netmarble Monster dives into the visual rendering techniques used to bring Mongil: Star Dive’s subcultural environments to life.

Watch as he shares insights from the development process, focusing on shader optimization, GPU-based performance enhancements, and the architecture of the visual system, and explore how complex mathematical principles were applied to balance artistic fidelity with real-time performance—pushing boundaries and setting new benchmarks for visual quality in gaming. 

The session also highlights the unique challenges of rendering culturally rich, stylized visuals and the innovative solutions that enabled their success.

Find out more about creating games in Unreal Engine here: unrealengine.com/uses/games

title: Amplifying the Unreal Audio Engine With Extensions and Plugins | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, SweejTech explores the many ways developers can add to audio functionality in UE projects, touching on MetaSounds nodes and interfaces, the Builder API, audio subsystems, editor windows, source data overrides, feature plugins, bus effects, and unit tests. 

The session also shows how SweejTech are making use of these extension points to speed up audio workflows in Unreal Engine.

The session describes the development process of audio features like HDR, ambience, global parameters, and reverb with UE5’s numerous extension points in mind. It also covers case studies that highlight various extension setups within prototypes, and explores decisions made regarding which to use for production. 

The session concludes with a discussion of an approach to extending UE5 audio, one that can scale from small projects to the types of large-scale games that demand the most from Audio Engine extensions. 

Find out more about audio in Unreal Engine

title: Low-Level Development Using UE and the Latest Gaming Platforms | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, Adam Creighton and Kevin Nappoly of Enduring Games provide a high-level summary of low-level implementations and differences in development required to add the latest gaming platforms to concurrent development, with examples of in-development or just-released games. 

This session is designed for seasoned game teams making diverse content with UE5, to give considerations to help them avoid pitfalls and continually push the power of Unreal Engine to release more content for concurrent platforms, all with unified pipelines.

Topics covered include considerations for asset and graphics pipelines, render models, unique features in UE (and alternatives when not supported for the target platforms), and concurrent multiplatform development.

Find out more about using Unreal Engine to create games here: unrealengine.com/uses/games

Topics covered include mobile-specific features like touch inputs and device configurations, leveraging Blueprints, and exploring key metrics for performance optimization. 

We also peek under the hood to provide an understanding of how Unreal Engine is built.

Find out more about Unreal Engine for mobile game development here: unrealengine.com/uses/mobile-games

title: Capturing Military Doctrine in Behavior Trees Using LLMs | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, Paul Foster of Lockheed Martin and Gita Sukthankar of UCF discuss in-progress work of an Unreal Engine plugin that provides an interactive chat that works alongside the Behavior Tree editor in the Unreal Editor. 

Military doctrine refers to the guidelines that govern how military forces participate in various types of operations, from campaigns and battles to engagements. By leveraging large language models (LLMs), developers can create a model that understands these guidelines and assists developers in creating behavior trees or state trees that accurately capture military doctrine within the Unreal Engine Game AI framework, including real-world scenarios for training.

By building on research from the University of Central Florida and utilizing behavior tree examples from the robotics industry, we can make the authoring of behavior trees for individual agents and multi-agent systems more efficient and realistic, and less labor-in
author: Unknown

title: Bringing Illumination’s Villain-Con Minion Blast to Life With UE | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, Universal Creative reveal how they generated feature-film-quality animation running in real time on the attraction 'Illumination’s Villain-Con Minion Blast', an interactive blaster game for all ages.

Explore the journey and challenges of converting film-quality characters to game-ready assets with zero quality loss, see the comparison of concept image and final rendered 3D scene, and enjoy a showcase of advanced environment lighting in Unreal Engine.

The team also outlines the successes and learnings of creating a real-time attraction on a moving walkway with up to 16 people in a room, the design of boss fights (including fighting engaging bosses in an infinite loop), and the graphics hardware used to achieve the amazing visuals using Unreal Engine on the attraction.

Learn more about Unreal Engine here: unrealengine.com

title: The State of Unreal for AECO | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:

The future of content creation isn't just about making great assets—it's about maximizing their potential across every possible platform and medium. 

Spacestation Animation, a digital entertainment studio founded by YouTube Pioneer 'Shonduras', reaches millions of young viewers across multiple platforms with their flagship property A for Adley family cartoon, demonstrating the power of their transmedia or ""re-imagination"" approach. 

Using Unreal Engine as their primary tool, they've developed innovative workflows that enable them to efficiently create and adapt content across various media formats while maintaining quality and brand consistency.

title: Developing and Launching a New Replication System | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, we dive into the design behind the Iris replication system, an opt-in replication system that works alongside Unreal Engine's existing replication system. 

You'll learn about the compromises made during design to remain as backward-compatible as possible, and about the most efficient path for migrating your existing serialization, replication graph code, and configuration to Iris. 

Topics covered in the session include a tour of the core components of Iris such as prioritization and filtering, and how to maximize backward compatibility and performance using these systems. 

Learn about the new serialization path using NetSerializers, and their benefits and differences to the existing serialization. The session also includes a look at tools, tips, and tricks for debugging bandwidth to optimize performance and maximize the gameplay experience. You'll also find out about new features coming to Iris in the future.

description:
Discover how exceptional production value was achieved for the world’s largest car company by integrating emerging technologies with an established Unreal Engine pipeline. 

Rotor Studios recently implemented an innovative hybrid post-production process to deliver a substantial amount of high-quality CG content for two global car launches, operating under both tight budgets and deadlines. Rotor augmented UE’s powerful Procedural Content Generation Framework (PCG) with Gaussian Splats for additional rapid, photorealistic 3D environment creation. Generative AI was also used to create important additional content for both video and still imagery.   

Join Scott Bradley of Rotor Studios for a detailed look at how this new workflow helps tackle specific issues like limited locations, time constraints, and shifting client briefs to maximize production dollars and deliver high-quality results. The session features real-world examples and practical techniques successfully applied to in-market

This session starts with an introduction to typical multiplayer game architecture and a discussion of what Unreal Engine best practices do and don't cover. Next up are challenges observed at previous studios and how Gardens approached these challenges.

Learn about the issues Alamode solves using technology like Docker and zero-trust VPNs and hear about current use cases.

title: Transforming Infrastructure Design With Unreal Engine Tools | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, infrastructure design giant HNTB explores how Unreal Engine enables them to create flexible and immersive visualizations for large-scale infrastructure projects. 

Topics include HNTB's custom Datasmith pipeline for importing GIS data and integrating their material pipeline, an interactive callout and chart system, and data-driven tools for construction sequences. 

HNTB's Python editor tools enhance Perforce integration and material creation, and expand customization of PCG foliage with OpenCV. Custom material graphs and HLSL shaders enable their artists to improve fidelity, introduce randomization, and address UV issues directly within Unreal Engine without constant round trips between other software. 

Finally, the session showcases HNTB's post-process materials for creating stylized environments, object highlighting, and custom mattes for compositing.

Find out more about architectural visualization in Unreal Engine here: unreal
author: Unknown

title: Automate and Expand Sequencer’s Functionality with Python | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, Daniel Orozco of Sony Pictures Imageworks explores the exciting results the company has achieved via Python integration with Unreal Engine’s Sequencer. 

Despite the creative nature of content creation in a VFX environment, users often go through repetitive actions to achieve their artistic vision. After manually doing processes in Sequencer like splitting subsequences, binding several tracks to the same camera, or inserting a shot in the middle of the sequence, a question arises: "Could this be done with a tool?" Thanks to Unreal's Python integration, the answer is, "Yes!" 

This session covers some of the tools Sony Pictures Imageworks developed for layout work in Unreal's Sequencer, such as prototyping and iterating tools. It also presents common concepts and considerations for optimizing the artist's workflow while still complying with the studio pipeline.

Find out more about Sequencer in Unreal Engine here: dev.epicgames.com/d

description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, we explore the best practices for using Horde: a set of services from Epic Games, designed to support workflows for developing Fortnite, Unreal Engine, and other projects. 

Horde includes functionality for remote execution, build and test automation, and mobile/console device management, among other services. This talk dives into the approaches used in Fortnite and other Epic Games projects to minimize build times, build costs, build breakages, and time broken.

Learn how Epic sets up Horde for our own projects to maximize throughput and maintainability, touching on how we use author-performant build graphs, optimize resourcing, get the most from Horde's build health tool, and work with branching techniques.

Find out more about Horde in Unreal Engine here: dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/horde-in-unreal-engine

Geotech, as an official Epic Games development partner, helped architect and develop Unreal Engine’s Motion Design tool from the start, and remain active contributors to its evolution.

In 2024, in collaboration with Emissive Labs, Geotech took the Motion Design Toolset to the next level by developing a live-events application, venue4D, designed to run Unreal Engine motion graphics in stadiums and arenas.

Denys and Danny demonstrate how to package your motion design project and generate a game build; control scenes in a packaged game using network APIs; optimize performance for demanding scenarios; and implement your own extensions and package them for distribution. 

Denys also shows how to apply AAA game development best practices to motion design and real-time graphics for media & entertainment.

Learn more about Unreal Engine here

title: Converting Blueprints the Right Way | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, Amazon Games explores how to convert Blueprints to C++ code effectively. 

Wouldn't it be great to have a button you could click to convert a Blueprint to C++, one that updates your entire project instantly, and leaves it in a fully compiled and runnable state?

Everyone knows that converting Blueprints manually is tedious and highly error-prone, often to the point where you can’t justify the effort and simply live with the problem. However, after a while it can’t be avoided any longer due to performance issues or overly complex Blueprints that are hard to maintain. And typically this comes very late in development—the worst possible time.  Ironically, when conversion begins, everyone focuses on the C++ part of the process, which is the easy part. The hard parts are often ignored or left as-is.

title: AI in Action: Transforming UE Workflows with AI Tools | Unreal Fest Orlando 2025
description:
In this session recorded at Unreal Fest Orlando 2025, Luis Placid and Shazzy Gustafson of ICVR provide an in-depth look at how publicly available AI tools can drastically accelerate 3D content creation for Unreal Engine—and explore areas where it still falls short.

This case study shows how a handcrafted Unreal Engine scene was recreated from the ground up using AI tools and workflows. The session highlights the most effective generative AI use cases, as well as the areas where AI struggled to match the original handcrafted quality benchmark, including 2D-to-3D character generation, environment creation with neural splats, automated character rigging, and AI-driven animation. 

Whether you're an artist, developer, technical director, or creative, this talk aims to demystify AI workflows in Unreal Engine, highlight various challenges and solutions, and show where and how you can begin leveraging these tools today to unlock new creative possibilities for you and your team.

title: Working with Animation Data in Unreal Engine 5.6 | A-COM Animation Sample | Lesson 2
description:
Welcome to Course Two! This module set empowers you to take absolute control of your motion assets, making your workflow flexible and non-destructive.
We begin with data mobility, learning to move seamlessly between live Control Rigs and baked Animation Sequences by mastering baking and the backward solve feature.
Next, you will integrate Layered Control Rigs to make non-destructive changes and tweaks directly on top of existing animation data. We then master Animation Layers to isolate specific motions (like camera shake) and precisely control their influence using the weight slider.
Finally, dive into the Keyframe Curve Editor. You will utilize essential tools like Buffer Curves (your animation safety net), the Euler filter (for rotations), and powerful mass keyframe editing features (including the bake tool for density reduction) to clean and polish complex motion data. Get ready to animate with unparalleled precision!

title: You’re Probably Lighting Wrong: A Guide to Physically Based Lighting in Unreal Engine 5 | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
Join Sean Gobey for an end-to-end overview on lighting and how to make your projects shine in Unreal Engine.

Unreal Engine has wonderful physically accurate lighting and camera systems yet most developers don't fully understand how to get the most out of them. For example, the default directional light value is 6 lux, yet the sun is 120,000 lux. 

So what does 6 mean? Where does this value come from and how do we tune the rest of the system if we're working with arbitrary numbers? If we're not introducing enough light, how does that affect our camera settings? 

With this value, we're now using an ISO of 50,000 to get an exposure. We can certainly build a pipeline around these arbitrary numbers, but what does this mean for new artists joining our team? Swing by for answers to all these questions—and many more.

What happens when you put a live performer into Unreal Engine? What happens when you bring real-time performance to a physical venue with a live audience? What opportunities does Unreal Engine provide for games, music, and live performance to unite? 

In this session, you’ll hear how musician and former triple j presenter Sally Coleman created animated sci-fi band Big Sand using Unreal Engine, motion capture, streaming, and networking techniques. Big Sand’s first live shows have been world-first experiments using out-of-the box applications of Unreal Engine for live audiences.
author: Unknown

title: Game-Changing Inputs: Navigating Enhanced Input in Unreal Engine and Conquering Common Challenges | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
In this comprehensive session on Enhanced Input in Unreal Engine, we'll guide attendees through the essential setup process, briefly compare against the legacy input system, and explore advanced implementation techniques. 

Starting with a foundational overview, we'll swiftly navigate through the setup intricacies to ensure a seamless integration into your projects. Delving deeper, we'll speak about our previously successful methodologies used across various projects, focusing on scalability and compatibility with diverse peripherals, and discuss the decision-making process behind different input solutions for distinct user groups, ensuring an intuitive experience. 

We’ll then look at how the Lyra starter game implements some of its more interesting Enhanced Input functionality, and we'll showcase strategies and best practices that can be used in other projects.
author: Unknown

title: Tips and Tricks for Chaos Destruction | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description: In this presentation, Technical Artist Xiao Yue dives into how to make destruction effects more realistic and how to control them in game while keeping high-end destruction performant.
author: Unknown

title: The Journey from mGear to ueGear: a Pythonic Postmortem | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
In this talk, mcsGear Studios will explain their processes and findings from writing the current version on ueGear and mGear. 

They’ll cover what they had planned to implement, how they went about implementing it, and the learnings they discovered along the way. 

mcsGear will focus on going deep into using Python with Unreal Engine, demonstrating that TDs and pipeline engineers don’t need to steer clear of Unreal if they don’t know C++.
author: Unknown

title: Advanced Niagara VFX: Fluids, Simulation Stages, and More! | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description: In this presentation, Technical Artist Xiao Yue will walk through how to leverage the sim stage and some advanced data interfaces in Niagara to create various physics simulations. This includes exploring particle-based constraints and grid-based fluid effects. She’ll also share some exciting updates on the Niagara Fluids plugin.
author: Unknown

title: A Few Good Tools: How a Small Team of Engineers Can Make a Big Difference | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
Creating an atypical game in Unreal Engine requires some atypical workflows—and with atypical workflows come atypical problems. 

Accompanied by co-speaker Alissa Vovers, Summerfall Studios will look at several practical examples of tools they created during the development of Stray Gods: the Roleplaying Musical to tackle some of these problems where they weren't able to leverage existing Unreal Engine tools to their full potential. 

We’ll discover how these tools empowered and supported the team, allowing them to create content at a scale much larger than they would have been able to otherwise.
author: Unknown

title: Using Unreal Automation at Riot Games: Make Unreal Do the Work for You | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description: This talk will give an overview of the three main components of automation in Unreal Engine: Unreal Automation Tool (UAT), Unreal Build Tool (UBT), and Build Graph. We will demonstrate how these can be used to automate and augment developers' workflows. This will be demonstrated with a practical example using automation tests in Unreal Engine.
author: Unknown

title: How to Benefit from Multithreading in Your Unreal Engine Projects | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description: Many more people could be benefiting from multithreading in their Unreal projects than are currently using it. Let's close that gap! Join Alex Stevens for an overview of multithreading, how to use it, and concrete examples with results in practice.
author: Unknown

title: Overlay Materials For Outlines and Other FX
description: A quick tutorial on how to create and apply a material using the Overlay parameter on meshes.
author: Unknown

title: Melee Hit Detection with No Compromises | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
In this session, Digital Confectioners will showcase a system they have developed that builds on the out-of-the-box systems Unreal Engine provides for tracing to provide a lag-redundant and highly performant melee hit-detection system for action games, where both collision accuracy and performance matter.

The talk will cover caching collision shapes/transform data from meshes and caching transform data from animations to build a system that can catch up on performing collision sweeps when lagging or hitching.

We’ll also look at the performance of the system including how to minimize the number of collision sweeps performed without losing accuracy; caching data upfront instead of re-fetching data; optimizing data for better CPU cache usage; and minimizing CPU cycles.
author: Unknown

title: Advanced Rendering and Debugging Tips for Unreal Engine 5 | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
With the new graphics capabilities in UE5, it’s now possible to achieve realistic graphics with relative ease—but many developers can still find themselves struggling to make adjustments for performance.

In this session, we’ll introduce graphics adjustment methods and development tips from a performance perspective, based on the daily queries our support team receives from developers.
author: Unknown

title: Advanced Blueprinting Techniques in Unreal Engine | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description: While so much is possible with Blueprints in Unreal Engine, you can quickly reach a point where you seemingly can't take it any further. Join Senior Technical Artist Matt Oztalay as he covers the frameworks, systems, and design paradigms to get the most out of the Blueprint visual scripting system.
author: Unknown

title: Exploring the Power of Control Rig for Animation in Unreal Engine 5.4 | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
In this session, we'll explore the Power of Control Rig to build advanced animation rigs in Unreal Engine 5.4.

We'll dive deep into Control Rig graphs, demonstrating various rigging approaches such as iterative solving, data-driven rigging, control interactions, and proxy controls.
Together, we'll build two rig modules for the new Modular Rigging framework, and go over the new Layered Control Rigs along all the latest animation features in Unreal Engine 5.4.
author: Unknown

title: TSR, Nanite, Lumen, VSM: UE5 Graphics Features Insights from Japan | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
UE5 includes a variety of new graphics technologies such as Nanite, Lumen, Temporal Super Resolution (TSR), and Virtual Shadow Maps (VSM).

In this session, Nori Shinoyama shares insights on these features based on his experience of supporting Japanese developers over the past several years.

This session will be useful as fundamental knowledge for those who want to create high-quality graphics using UE5, not only for games but also for VFX and other industries, too.
author: Unknown

title: Virtualize Everything: Polygons, Shadows, and Textures, Oh My! | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
With so much virtualization of large datasets available to you in Unreal Engine, it may seem daunting to consider all the possibilities and their implications for your pipelines.

In this talk, we’ll showcase some of the new features of Nanite; walk you through how to best leverage virtual textures in your project; explore how to tune virtual shadow maps to fit your memory and performance budgets; and finally, look at how to debug the memory usage of these features.
author: Unknown

title: Optimized MetaHumans and Cloth Workflows in Talisman | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description: Get an inside look at the optimizations made that enabled MetaHumans to be performant for Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN) in the Talisman demo shown at GDC 2024, and how you can apply these optimizations to your own MetaHuman characters. We’ll also dive into the new panel-based clothing system and how to make the most of it for your clothing needs.
author: Unknown

title: Exploring the New State Tree for AI | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description: This talk will explore the new experimental State Tree feature for AI development. Learn the strength and limitations of State Tree and its use case in comparison with the more mature Behavior Tree.
author: Unknown

title: Lighting the Path: Pathfinding for 60K Units in Age of Darkness | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
Join Playside Studios as they delve into the intricate development of navigation technology within the immersive world of Age of Darkness. 

Clinton Pinto and Jack Riddell will guide you through the fascinating journey of enabling 65,000 units to move and engage in synchronized combat, unveiling the secrets behind achieving seamless pathfinding at scale and mastering the complexities of unit formations within the fast-paced RTS environment of Age of Darkness. 

Learn about the innovative systems and technologies devised to overcome the challenges of orchestrating massive battles. Discover the implementation intricacies of our custom flow field pathfinding and the unforeseen design hurdles encountered while integrating formations into a survival game.
author: Unknown

title: Improving Development Iterations: A Deep Dive into Enhanced Features | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
As projects grow, we need to pay close attention to daily build times and development efficiency.

In this session, we’ll present a deep dive into the features that improve development iteration with a look at the mechanisms and use cases of core technologies such as Zen Series and UnrealCloudDDC.
author: Unknown

title: Tips and Tricks to Get Your Projects Shipping Faster! | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
In this talk, I discuss a range of topics spread across different domains that will help you produce and deliver games quicker.

- Using message bus systems to simplify subsystem communications.
- Common replication patterns, when to use them and how they work under the hood.
- Using the enhanced input system to simplify input handling.
- Using threads together with Blueprints to improve both performance and ease of content creation.
- Using Instanced Structs for simplifying data communication. 
- How to implement hotfixes into your game for rapid patching.
- Improving production pipelines through automation tools such as Jenkins and Unreal Game Sync.
- Improving the Steam Online Subsystem with handy features to improve production and QA flow.
author: Unknown

title: Implementing a Quality Cloud CI System Using Horde | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
In this talk, you’ll get an insight into Riot Games' journey into the implementation and migration to Epic’s Horde CI-CD system with examples of the efforts Riot has been investing in to make Horde the primary CI system for Unreal Engine games, as well of some of the challenges the team has faced.

Riot has focused on providing easy mechanisms for per-team Horde deployments that take advantage of infrastructure-and-configuration-as-code principles, as well as standard infrastructure templates for their commonly used Unreal Engine workflows.
author: Unknown

title: The Artist’s Guide to Editing the Editor: Automation, Validation, and Custom Tools | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
Are you scaling your art team toolsets in Unreal Engine? Are you looking to empower your team with better communication, workflows, and pipeline?

In this talk, we’ll dive into several Unreal Engine technologies and workflows such as Interchange for import and export, Editor Utility Widgets, managing asset data, customizing the Editor UI, and asset validation. Make sure you have your checklist ready to go before your next big project.
author: Unknown

title: Linear Content for YouTube: Learnings from The Amazing Digital Circus and Murder Drones | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
Glitch Productions is an indie animation company that distributes direct to audiences on YouTube with over eight million subscribers, five shows, and 720 millions collective views. In this session, Glitch will share learnings and pipeline advice from its shows The Amazing Digital Circus and Murder Drones.

Come along for an insight into creating stylised cartoon expressions for characters; lighting and rendering tips and tricks; advice on budgeting and planning; and much more.
author: Unknown

title: Black Magic Decklink Input to UE
description: Setting up Blackmagic Decklink media as media source in UE and how to configure with and without a Media Profile
author: Unknown

title: Game Framework Extensions: Four Deep Dives in Forty Minutes | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description: No fluff, just three general purpose extensions to the Engine, GameFramework, and Iris, that will improve the productivity and stability of your codebase. Each extension doubles as a technical deep dive into its domain, exposing the inner workings of Unreal Engine for you to harness for your specific needs.
author: Unknown

title: Animating Cinematics in Unreal: Lessons Learned from a Fortnite Animator | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description:
This session will dive into animating in engine to create epic cinematics. For newcomers to Unreal Engine, we’ll start with a basic overview of what animating in engine means. 

We’ll take a look at the pros and cons of working in Unreal Engine versus a more traditional animation software such as Maya. This talk covers the use of Sequencer and explores frequently used Unreal Engine Animation tools such as the Graph Editor, the Tween tool, Pose Library, constraints, and Control Rig.

Finally, we’ll do a deep dive into a Fortnite cinematic, which we’ll use as an example of how to set up a project in Unreal Engine and how to best structure your content to work collaboratively.
author: Unknown

title: How to Handle Input and Navigation in Unreal Motion Graphics (UMG) | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description: This talk will explore best practices for handling input and navigation in Unreal Motion Graphics (UMG). Attendees will be able to follow along with a live demo as we build out a mockup screen and use common UI paradigms to set up something quickly and efficiently.
author: Unknown

title: 20 Things You Should Be Using in Unreal Motion Graphics (UMG) | Unreal Fest Gold Coast 2024
description: You can achieve quite a lot by only knowing a little Unreal Motion Graphics (UMG), but it doesn't take long to realize it's a deep system. Join Adrienne Pugh for a live deep dive into some of the lesser-known features of UMG that you should be using in your own projects to save time and overhead.
author: Unknown

title: Epic Secondary Educator Summit- Oct 2024
description: Join us for our fall Epic Secondary Educator Summit on Oct 12, 2024. Our innovative lineup of educators will share the great work they’re doing integrating interactive 3D technology into their learning spaces. Interactive 3D content development is providing countless opportunities for students who want to explore new careers in film, games, advertising, architecture, engineering, and more. Throughout the summit, you’ll get to see how your peers are integrating this immersive technology in their curricula. In the process, they’ll help to demystify the tools behind this fast-growing technology, so you can learn how you can bring this technology to your students without the need to be an expert yourself.
author: Unknown

title: Getting Started with Deformers in UE 5.5
description: This tutorial walks you through the very basics of getting a deformer on your skeletal mesh in sequencer.
author: Unknown

title: Building HLODs through Horde
description: Building HLODs for games/experiences using the world partitioning system is best done if the process is offloaded to Horde. In this step-by-step process, I will show you how you can set up the HLOD building process on Horde.
author: Unknown

title: Chaos Visual Debugger - User Guide for UE 5.5
description: User Guide for the Beta release of the Chaos Visual Debugger for UE 5.5. The tool to Debug Physics in Unreal Engine
author: Unknown

title: Smooth apparition of instances with dithering
description: In this tutorial, we'll explore two interesting material nodes, PerInstanceFadeOutDistance and DitherTemporalAA, and see how to use them to create smooth apparition of instanced objects
author: Unknown

title: Expedition Planning by Quixel
description: Scheduling scan artists, transporting equipment to location, booking travel and accommodations, this course details the major considerations when planning a scan trip.
author: Unknown

title: Content Curation by Quixel
description: This course looks at what is involved in organizing assets into collections. From deciding target subjects to compiling digital assets into collections, this process is essential for asset management.
author: Unknown

title: Scouting by Quixel
description: Before heading out to a remote location and scanning whatever is available, effort should be made to ensure the location is ideal. This is the process of Scouting. This course details the scouting workflow and the tasks involved in choosing the perfect location to scan.
author: Unknown

title: The Game Dev Cave: Unity to Unreal Series
description: For any Unity developers out there, looking to switch over to Unreal Engine, there can be a lot of intimidating aspects to this move. This series is for Unity developers to learn to work with Unreal Engine!
author: Unknown

title: Myth-busting "Best Practices" in Unreal Engine
description:
Are Ticks really that problematic? Should you make all your meshes Nanite? Is the ChildActorComponent truly cursed? Should you never use Cast?
You've probably heard many of these so-called "best practices”. Let's put them to the test and find out which ones are true and which ones are bust.
author: Unknown

title: Visualizing complex products in Unreal: Keys To Success References
description: The foundational strategies of approaching the first steps to establishing a robust center of excellence in Unreal Engine as you establish your Product Visualization Platform in your organization.
author: Unknown

title: Transitioning Maya to Unreal for animators
description:
In this course, you’ll learn how to animate directly in Unreal Engine using Control Rig characters and prop actors within Sequencer to build full shots and explore workflows both new and familiar. With production-focused practices in mind, we’ll dive into the benefits of working with real-time authoring tools, while building off your prior experience in tools like Maya to make learning a new set of tools both smooth and exciting.

By the end of this course, you’ll be able to create and animate full sequences using any combination of keyframe animation techniques and motion capture workflows, through Level Sequences and Subsequences. You’ll also learn to use Unreal’s native authoring tools for animators, such as various Curve Editor features, a new Constraints system, Space Switching, and dynamic Control Rig features that will open the door to new ways of animating, as well as the ways you’re used to working.
author: Unknown

title: I Wish I Learned This Sooner! | Unreal Fest 2024
description: Quick tips and tricks covering a variety of foundational tools and techniques in Unreal Engine including: multigate for simple swapping of all kinds, Game Modes imported from templates, the power of boolean operations with the modeling tools, and the best shortcuts you still haven’t found.
author: Unknown

title: Gathering Unreal Insights Traces on Android
description: A step-by-step walkthrough for collecting Unreal Insights traces from a local Android device
author: Unknown

title: Efficient materials for large worlds
description: Improve the precision and performance of your materials with this one simple trick!
author: Unknown

title: Using Chaos Physics for Large-Scale and High-Fidelity Scenes | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
The Chaos Physics system—and destruction in particular—has seen many changes in 5.4. 

Advancements developed for Fortnite, UEFN MetaHumans with cloth, and more now enable more realistic, performant, and engaging experiences for players. 

This talk explores some of our new features and improvements coming to physics in Unreal Engine, including how we achieved dynamic destruction in a huge sandbox environment; building a pipeline for creating high-fidelity clothing for your characters; and putting together a new debugging framework for physics scenes and improved runtime performance and memory usage to allow for more dynamic and expressive simulation at larger scales.
author: Unknown

title: Unreal Engine 5 Character and Animation Optimizations | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
Dive into the many character and animation optimizations that you should be applying to your Unreal Engine 5 projects to ensure you are delivering a fluid 60 frames per second on consoles. 

This talk will examine building from the fundamentals through to advanced methods, as we explore optimizations of animations, skeletal meshes, animation graphs, state machines, and more. Along the way, we’ll discover many hidden features and techniques that will enable you to squeeze as much performance out of your characters and animation as possible.
author: Unknown

title: Real-Time 3D HMI for the High-End Yacht Industry | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
In this session, Applied will showcase how they developed and delivered HMI software for the luxury yacht industry.

Explore how the team used Unreal Engine to develop a 3D application installed on a touchscreen in the cockpit of the yacht that enables the crew to see a 3D visualization of the boat and control the status of more than 600 variables of the vessel’s various systems.
  
This session will demonstrate to manufacturers and developers how it’s possible to use UE to build complex and mission-critical HMIs—and that this is not only achievable by big and established companies but also by smaller teams without compromising on quality, complexity, and functionality.
author: Unknown

title: Procedurally Generating Level Sequences from a Dialogue Script | Unreal Fest 2024
description: During this session, Big Bad Wolf Studio will present a tool developed for Vampire the Masquerade: Swansong which procedurally generates level sequences from dialogue scripts that are automatically created and filled with camera cuts, animations, sounds, and various events to handle subtitles, jumps between sequences, and conditions.
author: Unknown

title: Optimizing Survival Games for Mobile | Unreal Fest 2024
description: In this session, we will cover the latest optimizations in Unreal Engine 5.4 for open world survival games on mobile. Join us to hear about new features for lighting in mobile survival games, GPU scene optimizations for mobile, memory insights for Android, mobile iteration time improvements, and various other CPU and GPU optimizations.
author: Unknown

title: Import Customization through the Interchange Framework | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
In this session, we’ll give an introduction to the Interchange Framework covering its basis, philosophy, new UI, option configurability, and overall settings. 

There will be an advanced section on gleaning insights on the pipeline process and the creation of custom pipeline stack and pipelines with user-specific behavior.
author: Unknown

title: How We Used The Gameplay Ability System in UE for ‘Outriders: Worldslayer’ | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
In this session,  People Can Fly will show you how they developed character skills with Blueprints using the Gameplay Ability System in Unreal Engine for Outriders: Worldslayer. 

They’ll dive into the workings of the Gameplay Ability System, demonstrating how easy it is to manage dependencies between skills and how to prepare a skill to facilitate the work of other teams (such as VFX and sound). 

Attendees will learn about the pros and cons of the system, as well as how to augment it and what to watch out for. 

The session will include examples of things People Can Fly were unable to implement using the system and how they hacked it.
author: Unknown

title: How to Build an Open World Game with 4,000 Strangers | Unreal Fest 2024
description: In March, Epic launched Project Titan, a global collaborative game jam in which over 4,000 people signed up to build a massive 8x8km game world. In this talk, we explore the development of the project, the tools used to create and support it, and the back-end infrastructure that made it all possible.
author: Unknown

title: Modular Rigging in Unreal Engine | Unreal Fest 2024
description: In this talk, we'll take a look at how UE 5.4's modular rigging features can speed up character creation and empower artists to get creative.
author: Unknown

title: Exploring the Next-Generation Animation Tools in UE 5.4 | Unreal Fest 2024
description: In this talk, you’ll learn how to create robust animation directly in engine to bring your assets to life. We’ll explore new animation features and techniques with Unreal Engine 5.4 including Control Rig, retargeting, Sequencer, Deformer Graph, and the Skeletal Editor.
author: Unknown

title: Amsterdam ZuidasDOK: A Digital Twin Platform Built on UE 5.4 | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
Behold the dynamic digital replica of Amsterdam's illustrious financial hub, intricately crafted to be navigated effortlessly through touch panel, mouse, or seamlessly managed remotely via web interface.

In this session, VERO Agency will leverage their experience with Amsterdam ZuidasDOK to discuss how to build in Unreal Engine at city scale without losing top-tier quality, speed, or performance. 

VERO will also look at the process of integrating different kinds of 3D sources into one unified masterplan experience; the seamless integration of dynamic data to enhance the depth and richness of your experience; and how to tailor the technology to suit a myriad of diverse cases and usage scenarios.
author: Unknown

title: An Artist’s Guide to Using Nanite Tessellation | Unreal Fest 2024
description: In this talk, we explore the new Nanite features for UE 5.4 and look at best practices to keep in mind when building with Nanite. This artist-focused session will cover everything you need to know to create Nanite meshes that run well and don't blow your memory budget.
author: Unknown

title: Blurring the Lines between Animation and Gaming with Unreal Engine and Fortnite | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
In this talk, film and game director HaZ Dulull will give us a deep dive into how he and his team at production company HaZimation took a strategic approach to transmedia when producing original content for film and games, and how one IP turned into a Fortnite game—Moontopia—using UEFN. 

This session will break down how HaZimation were able to pivot from animated series development into a game IP thanks to UEFN / Fortnite.
author: Unknown

title: Designing and Implementing Your Game’s AI Architecture in Unreal Engine | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
In this session, 11 bit studios will present a case study on designing and implementing a flexible framework for AI characters in a TPP stealth-action title using Unreal Engine.  

They will go through how they approached each stage and the different challenges they had to overcome,  focusing on why and how to combine different AI techniques like behavior trees, state machines, utility theory, and rule-based systems into a cohesive framework in Unreal Engine that has all the advantages but none of the disadvantages of each of those techniques, and what new considerations it might create.
author: Unknown

title: A Taste of Chocolate: Adding a Rendering Fast Path without Breaking Unreal Engine | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
Faced with the challenge of building massive environments from over 60,000 mesh components, including fields of real-time simulated debris, the engineering team at Creative Assembly needed to find a way to reduce level streaming costs and optimize rendering of unique instances.  

In this talk, Grant Johnson, Senior Graphics and Engine Programmer at Creative Assembly, will look back at the problems the team faced building these environments in a multiplayer first-person shooter set in space, as well as diving into their solution (dubbed ‘Chocolate Rendering’): a modern geometry renderer injected directly into the engine. 

Presentation Links:

PDF: https://drive.google.com/file/d/16UZsfL2KZ21YbpQBEjzm1br6CCfVYCLD/view

PowerPoint: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_gp5qQqMfB3nR6c9VO4JvrJaEerum1OG/view
author: Unknown

title: XR Streaming and Digital Twins: Enabling an Open Infrastructure Metaverse | Unreal Fest 2024
description: The talk will demonstrate how Bentley's iTwin plugin works with Innoactive's  XR content management platform, guiding you through a simple workflow to produce highly performant, immersive experiences for your customers. Starting with streaming BIM and CAD data into Unreal Engine from various sources or design tools, followed by the creation of compelling and interactive content for uses within architectural visualisation, training, simulation and more. Then you will learn how to effortlessly deploy the scenarios to VR headsets or stream directly to a browser.
author: Unknown

title: Using Simple Generic Materials to Improve UI Performance | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
This talk is based on Virtuos Labs’ work on an unannounced UE5 AAA title that is currently in production. 

The presentation will showcase simple, reusable materials that have enabled Virtuos  to replace traditional layout methods in the UI. This helps them to avoid using panels and render transforms in the UI, enabling them to manage performance between the CPU and the GPU depending on the use case. 

Swing by to learn how to use materials as a reliable alternative to the optimization suggestions outlined in the Unreal Motion Graphics (UMG) documentation.
author: Unknown

title: PCG: First Steps to Advanced Development
description: PCG caught the Unreal Engine community by storm with 5.2 but it left quite a few people only scratching the surface. In this session Chris Murphy briefly covers the basics of PCG then dives into some of the advanced techniques to help you further your PCG dreams.
author: Unknown

title: Automating Innovation: Real-Time Experiences with 3DEXCITE | Unreal Fest 2024
description: Discover how 3DEXCITE uses Unreal Engine to drive real-time experiences with 3DEXCITE create & show. Learn about the usage of openUSD and MaterialX for efficient automated interchange of virtual twins running on the cloud using Unreal Engine’s Vulkan RHI. In this talk you will see how automation elevates our realtime cloud services to deliver immersive, high-quality experiences.
author: Unknown

title: The Triumphs and Travails of Making a Stylized Cartoon in UE5 Based on Lil’ Ruby | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
This session will explore the challenges Platige Studio had to overcome during the production of the nine-minute stylized animated film Lil' Ruby in Unreal Engine.  At the project's inception, there were no real tools or clear paths to complete it efficiently.  Attendees will hear how solutions were devised on the fly in response to emerging needs and challenges. 

Additionally, attendees will:

- Come away understanding the general challenges that should be expected when making stylized animation in UE in a studio environment, both from a production and technology perspective. 

- Learn the tools and solutions used to achieve a stylized 2D look in Lil’ Ruby. 

- Get a look at the pipeline for handling over 130 shots between the previs/animation/lighting phases as well as the benefits of using UE versus a regular Maya/Arnold-based pipeline.
author: Unknown

title: Workflow Best Practices & Avoiding Common Pitfalls with Perforce & Unreal Engine | Unreal Fest 2024
description: In this session, Ryan Maffesoli, Sr. Solutions Engineer at Perforce, will demonstrate workflow best practices and common pitfalls seen through Helix Core and Unreal Engine deployments for studios big and small — including his admin support of Epic’s 4000-person global art jam (Project Titan). Ryan will teach you all the save-your-bacon tools, tips, and techniques he’s learned over the years, so that you can improve your onboarding and keep your creative projects running smoothly and securely.
author: Unknown

title: Jelly by Name, Jelly by Nature: A Deep Dive into Deforming Characters in UE 5.3 | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
This focused discussion will explore the challenges and solutions involved in character deformation in Unreal Engine. Explore Brown Bag Films transition from a traditional Maya animation pipeline to an in-engine animation pipeline leveraging the real-time animation capabilities offered by Unreal 5.3.
 
Central to this talk is the character Jelly, whose unique deformation requirements—ranging from  squash and stretch to melting transformations—presented both challenges and learning  opportunities for creative problem-solving.
author: Unknown

title: Optimizing the Game Thread | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
In this talk, Tanglewood Games will dive into the Game Thread in UE5 and explore how we can profile and optimize this.

Jake Simpson, Intermediate Programmer and Associate Lead at Tanglewood Games, will illustrate common issues using examples seen in real projects.

Using Unreal Insights, Jake will identify some of the common performance issues found in Unreal game projects and techniques that can help to get your timings down across the Game Thread, based on personal experiences.  

By the end of this talk, you’ll know how to identify a number of problems on the Game Thread and how you can diagnose and fix these.
author: Unknown

title: Breaking Down Walls: Merging Traditional Art Departments with Virtual Production | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
Imagine an Art Department on a film or TV series where walls crumble, not literally, of course, but conceptually. Where the tools you rely on (SketchUp Pro, Rhino) seamlessly integrate with the power of Unreal Engine (UE) and Twinmotion. This isn't just about virtual production; it's about a complete revolution.

My vision is a unified Art Department. A place where assets flow effortlessly from concept art and pre-vis to final construction drawings and VFX. A dynamic workflow that bounces between UE/Twinmotion/Twinmotion Cloud and ultimately back to SketchUp using Datasmith for live updates. This approach eliminates the traditional bottlenecks, fostering a truly collaborative environment.

But how do you, the designer already wielding SketchUp like a pro, bridge the gap to UE? Fear not! This session is designed to empower you. We'll show you how your existing design skills are the secret weapon you already possess.
author: Unknown

title: An Introduction to the Mover Plugin | Unreal Fest 2024
description: The recently released Mover plugin is an experimental tool supporting movement of actors with rollback networking. In this session, we will  discuss its high-level concepts, compare it with CharacterMovementComponent, take a look at what's running under the hood, and see what's planned for future development. Please note the README documentation file was missing from the initial 5.4 release -- but will be included in the 5.4.4 hotfix.

In this talk, Tanglewood Games will present how to add extra functionality to the Unreal Editor by leveraging its existing framework, enabling the creation of tools that feel native and intuitive to use, and that are tailored to custom projects, modular, and easy to maintain.   

These frameworks will be presented through a series of practical examples using both Blueprints and C++, ranging from simpler tasks like Editor Utility Widgets, Scriptable Actions, and Data Validators, to more advanced uses such as Slate Notifications, Component Visualizers, custom Details Panels and Editor Modes, and finally Asset Factories with Custom Viewports.

title: De-spaghetti Your Blueprints, the Scientific Way | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
It's well known that Blueprint visual scripting in Unreal Engine can get out of hand as a project evolves. The software industry has battled the same difficulties since the 80s so there are a couple of established scientific ways to measure and deal with code complexity.

Join Valentin Galea of Hangar 13 Games for a session that explores how Blueprints can benefit from concepts such as cyclomatic and Halstead complexity or the maintainability index.

He’ll show practical ways to integrate these metrics into Blueprint nodes and what kind of measuring thresholds are useful in day-to-day development.

He will also cover Data Validation and additional ways to keep complexity in check.
author: Unknown

title: Completing the Illusion: Accurate Depth of Field in ICVFX | Unreal Fest 2024
description:
Depth of field has long been tricky to manage in ICVFX—with either not enough blur on the wall or too much, what is the correct amount? Incorrect depth of field is one of the main culprits of LED wall shots looking obvious.

In this session, we’ll explore how Unreal Engine 5.4 has the answer with the new ICVFX Depth of Field Compensation feature. Solution Architect Ben Kidd will take you through this game changing tool and share with you everything learned along the way. Sharpen your on set knowledge and focus on achieving the most realistic shots with this fascinating deep dive.
author: Unknown

title: BMW Driving Simulator: Powered by Unreal Engine | Unreal Fest 2024

With over 14 simulators and usability labs, the BMW Group is creating every opportunity for its vehicle research and development engineers to simulate and test future product requirements under realistic conditions. Over the past few years, the automotive giant has converted to Unreal Engine for the simulators’ visualization capabilities. This talk will explore the learnings and highlights from that journey.

This session is a travel guide for brave animators who are about to embark on a journey into the world of Unreal Engine. Join us to prepare yourself for the best trip, understand what to expect, anticipate any struggles, and get excited—because you’re going to love it. 

Dimension will give an insight into how they have customized workflows and developed tools to help and support animators working in engine.

The talk will include an introduction to Unreal Engine for traditional 3D animators using Maya looking at the parallels between the two worlds as well as the differences. 


You’ll learn about the UE animation philosophy and its linear content production workflows, and there will also be practical tips on workflows unique to UE that can open new animation routines.

This session is designed for traditional 3D animators and previs artists who haven't started animating in UE yet, as well as those who have (but are still finding their way through).

title: Star Wars: Hunters by Natural Motion | State of Unreal | GDC 2024
description: Natural Motion provided an all-new look at Star Wars: Hunters, their arena-based online multiplayer game coming to Nintendo Switch, iOS, and Android. Zynga showed how they are using Unreal Engine to craft a high quality mobile experience both in gameplay and visual fidelity, and to deliver a game that is an authentic addition of the Star Wars universe.
author: Unknown

title: Chrono Odyssey by Chrono Studios | State of Unreal | GDC 2024
description: Chrono Studio revealed a new trailer from Chrono Odyssey, their MMORPG set in the vast open world of Setera, where players will fight various opponents and have a distinct sense of control over battles and progression through a unique time travel mechanic. Chrono Odyssey, published globally by Kakao Games, will be released for PC and consoles, and the team announced that it is coming to the Epic Games Store: https://store.epicgames.com/
author: Unknown

title: Dune: Awakening by Funcom | State of Unreal | GDC 2024
description:
Funcom delved into the mechanics of their open-world survival game Dune: Awakening, inspired by Denis Villeneuve's record-breaking and critically acclaimed Dune films, which are based on Frank Herbert's novels. Funcom also shared how two time Academy Award-winning cinematographer Greig Fraser used Unreal Engine for planning and pre-production on Dune: Part Two, illustrating how storytelling processes behind making films and games continue to merge. Check out the behind-the-scenes video, Dune: Awakening - Creating Worlds, From Book to Film to Game:  https://youtu.be/LW6ou6mugAA?si=w8Igx_F7lzCp9krc
